full_judgment: 11. Learned Advocate further contends that charge and also conviction and sentence vide impugned judgment and order under section 412 Penal Code against the accused-appellants Toyeb Ali, Gazi Rahman, Fazlul Haque and A Barek cannot be legally sustainable as the appellants being participants in the commission of the offence under section 395 Penal Code cannot be legally liable under section 412 Penal Code even if looted articles be available in their possession. He also contends that there being no positive evidence at the trial as to carrying definite deadly weapons during occurrence by each of the convict-appellants, conviction under section 397 Penal Code against them will be illegal. He submits that some of the CS witnesses were withheld without explanation and, according, to him above non-examination will bring presumption against prosecution under section 114g Evidence Act. He argues that statements under section 342 CrPC against appellant Toyeb Ali, Gazi Rahman and Barek were not recorded quite in accordance with law and, as such, the appellants were seriously prejudiced.
